hazard: Lack of antenatal screening for GBS

promises.quote: The UK NSC will be reviewing the evidence for antenatal screening for GBS again in 2015/16 as part of its routine evidence review process.

promises.quote: we will keep our recommendations under review, pending new evidence emerging.

concerns.quote: That antenatal screening for GBS is not routinely offered by the NHS, to all pregnant women, during the final weeks of pregnancy.
concerns.hazard: lack of antenatal screening for GBS

concerns.quote: That prophylactic intrapartum antibiotics are not routinely offered to all women who test positive for GBS (or have done so in the past).
concerns.hazard: lack of prophylactic intrapartum antibiotics for GBS-positive women

concerns.quote: That GBS infection is a very serious illness and in the absence of a national screening and prophylactic treatment programme, babies are potentially being put at risk of harm/death.
concerns.hazard: risk of GBS infection in newborns

promises.quote: the RCPCH is unable to comment on the specifics of the case and the Pennine Acute Hospitals NHS Trust has been asked to respond directly on local communication, record keeping and policies and procedures.
promises.summary: RCPCH will not comment on specifics; Trust to respond on communication, record keeping, and policies.

concerns.quote: That antenatal screening for GBS was not being routinely offered by the NHS to all pregnant - women during the final weeks of pregnancy
concerns.hazard: lack of antenatal screening for group B streptococcus

concerns.quote: Staff did not follow the Trust's protocols/guidance and did not document their rationale where - they exercised clinical discretion
concerns.hazard: inadequate communication handover and record keeping

concerns.quote: Midwives did not carry out a speculum examination, on two separate occasions, in order to - establish whether there had been a rupture of membranes
concerns.hazard: failure to assess rupture of membranes

concerns.quote: Neonatal observations were not carried out when it became apparent that there had been a - material change in baby's condition
Maternal observations were not carried out after delivery, despite a spike in temperature
Midwives did not escalate to or consult with the Obstetrician/Paediatrician/Neonatologist

links.explanation: Both reports highlight that antenatal screening for group B streptococcus (GBS) is not routinely offered to all pregnant women during the final weeks of pregnancy. They describe the same specific hazard and the same mechanism of potential harm to babies.
